static_traits.name: Lin Mutong
static_traits.social_status: Has a partner and some close friends to confide in, but they do not fully understand the impact of commuting on mental health
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior psychotherapy; never had similar stress issues before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe commuting stress, negative thoughts, and bodily reactions specifically; attitude rather negative and skeptical about change, but willing to try; cooperativeness acceptable; speech rate and logic features Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: My one-hour daily commute leaves me stressed and overwhelmed, generating negative thoughts and hopelessness. These feelings appeared and intensified since starting this Work six months ago; now every day Before work I dread driving, affecting my mood and Work efficiency; it sometimes happens on the way home too. I have tried listening to music and podcasts during the commute, but the negative thoughts persist.
basic_info.core_demands: 'I just want to feel a bit more at ease during the commute, not letting it ruin my mood before the day even begins.'

core_beliefs: I am trapped with no hope
I cannot change the current situation

special_situations.event: Every morning before leaving for work, thinking about needing to commute about an hour in congested traffic
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the commute is long and traffic is bad, my day is doomed to be bad, and my mood cannot Recover
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Listens to music or podcasts in the car trying to relieve stress and negative thinking
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Driving to work takes too long; I will never find Work closer to home

special_situations.event: When hitting severe traffic during the commute
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel intense Anxiety on the road, it means I cannot cope with this Work and the whole day will be ruined
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuing to use distracting methods (music, podcasts), but ignoring any slight improvement
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am trapped by this commute with no way out; it will ruin my whole day

special_situations.event: Arrives at the company already low in mood because of the commute, feeling behind on work progress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I arrive at the company in a bad mood, it means I will lag behind and perform poorly all day
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negative self-evaluation, ignores any positive feedback or achievements
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am always falling behind and cannot do Work well

special_situations.event: Moments when traffic is occasionally light and smooth
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Unless the commute is completely smooth, any slight improvement does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring brief moments of ease, not acknowledging their significance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Such relief is rare and useless

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain a sense of control and ease between commuting and work, keeping emotions stable
core_conflict.fear: Fearing the external situation cannot be changed, being trapped long-term by the fixed commuting structure, leading to persistent hopelessness and loss of control
defense_goal: Maintains pessimism and skepticism to reduce disappointment and avoid dashed expectations

object_relations.object_representation: Others who do not understand or cannot provide substantial help (colleagues, family, partner)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes adjusting cognition and reframing perspectives to reduce commuting stress
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes the external situation is fixed and unchanging, and psychological methods will not produce change (viewing change as impossible)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing 'I do not think there will be change' in a flat, skeptical tone, emphasizing the commute cannot change, minimizing further dialogue.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites identifying relatively less stressful moments or positive aspects
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing the commuting experience as all bad, with any slight improvement negated as meaningless
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using absolutist words (e.g. 'never''always'), negating positive moments, closing with firm but brief statements.

manifestations: Feeling trapped by the commuting structure, with no way out and no way to change; viewing each day's commute as fixed and uncontrollable

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: In counseling, repeatedly engages in negative self-evaluation with 'I am always falling behind'
Skeptical attitude toward change, cautiously expressing 'I am willing to try, but do not think it will help'
Difficulty acknowledging anything positive or momentary relief

exception_events.target_problem: Every morning before work and during the commute, the client usually experiences intense Anxiety and hopelessness, which then affects the whole day's mood and Work performance
exception_events.unique_outcome: At occasional moments when traffic is lighter and flow is smooth, the client feels slightly less stressed and experiences a bit of ease
exception_events.reason: Clue: different situation (less traffic, smoother flow, shorter commute), reduced external load created a deviation point of reduced stress this time

positive_force: Has had positive experiences and satisfaction with work
Willing to try new approaches and seek counseling support
Has basic support from a partner and friends (can confide)
Can notice stress easing when there is occasionally less traffic
negative_force: Long commuting time and traffic congestion; objective pressure persists
Mental filtering, overgeneralization, predicting the future and other cognitive biases reinforcing hopelessness
Sleep patterns disrupted by Anxiety, reducing resilience
Irritability leading to Relationship tension with colleagues and family
Negative-leaning self-evaluation, believing oneself 'constantly falling behind'

target_behavior.behavior: Significant Anxiety and dread before and after commuting, accompanied by increased heart rate, chest pressure, and irritability
antecedent: Hitting traffic congestion during the commute
On the way home after work
target_behavior.core_reason: High stress from long commutes and congestion triggering predictive thinking that 'things will not improve' and helplessness, with negative automatic thoughts repeatedly reinforcing Anxiety
target_behavior.function: Escaping and alleviating unwelcome Anxiety experiences, seeking temporary self-soothing (e.g. distracting with music/podcasts)
target_behavior.consequence: Affecting Work mood and productivity; more irritable interactions with colleagues and family; Sleep disturbance worsening the next day's stress experience
